content.title: Texas Water Crisis Threatens Booming Industrial Hotspot for Exxon, Koch
content.summary: Corpus Christi, a Gulf Coast city 400 miles (640 kilometers) south of Dallas, is in the grip of a worsening drought that’s already prompted lawn-watering bans and warnings that harsher restrictions may be necessary.  The city council recently halted work on a desalination plant that would have treated seawater after cost estimates spiraled to more than $1 billion and sparked outrage among some residents.  The issue also tapped into long-simmering resentment of the growing industrial presence of major water users such as Exxon Mobil Corp., Koch Industries LLC, Celanese Corp., and Occidental Petroleum Corp.

content.title: Energy sector is looking at gas more favorably than oil: Mizuho
content.description:
The analyst team out of Mizuho has upgraded Occidental Petroleum stock (OXY) from Neutral to Outperform as Wall Street is seeing an energy sector (XLE) pivot back into traditional energy, like oil (CL=F, BZ=F) and gas (RB=F).

Mizuho Americas managing director Nitin Kumar comes on Market Domination to speak more about this call and companies' exposure to various energy sources. Kumar also comments on the dealmaking and consolidation trends in the broader energy landscape.
